summary.plain: In 1979 the TASSO experiment at DESY's PETRA collider reported planar events in e+e- annihilation at high energies: collisions in which three jets of particles lie in one plane. Interpreted as a quark and an antiquark with a radiated gluon, this was the first direct evidence for the gluon.
summary.technical: TASSO paper 'Evidence for planar events in e⁺e⁻ annihilation at high energies' (Phys. Lett. B 86 (1979) 243): hard non-collinear gluon bremsstrahlung seen as planar three-jet topologies at PETRA energies above about 22 GeV. The first event (Event 13177, Run 447) was shown by B. Wiik at Neutrino 79, Bergen, on 18 June 1979; TASSO scientists Söding, Wiik, Wolf and Wu received the 1995 EPS HEPP Prize.

title: Evidence for planar events in e+e− annihilation at high energies
why_it_matters: DESY describes the three-jet events as the signature expected if a quark radiates a gluon, the carrier of the strong force; the four PETRA collaborations all showed three-jet analyses at the August 1979 Lepton-Photon Symposium.
